name: Penciljam Bengaluru at Chitrakala Parishath
description:
📆 22nd Nov 2026
⏱️ 11 am - 1 pm
📍 Karnataka Chitrakala Parishad

We are drawing at Karnataka Chitrakala Parishath.

Karnataka Chitrakala Parishath is a landmark institution in Bengaluru’s cultural landscape, founded in 1960 by art visionaries including Prof. M. S. Nanjunda Rao to promote and preserve the visual arts. Over more than six decades it has grown into a vibrant art complex with dozens of galleries showcasing traditional Mysore paintings, folk art, modern and contemporary works, as well as collections by celebrated artists like Nicholas and Svetoslav Roerich.
How to join this session
You don't need artistic skill to participate in this event - just boundless curiosity and a love for drawing. To connect with other participants, please use our community on Discord.
https://penciljam.com/main/community/

If this is your first time and would like future update on events, and more. Please register here.

Once you arrive at the location, choose a spot you'd like to sketch and get comfortable.
Things to carry for this session

 	A sketchbook/paper/drawing surface
 	Pencils or any medium you would like to try out
 	A portable chair/mat. If the location has no seating, we tend to sit on the ground
 	Water bottle and snacks

How to get there
Follow the location map provided

name: A new Way of Seeing: Sketch Journaling at MAP
description:
What if you could turn a visit to an exhibition into an opportunity to document your own observations, thoughts and discoveries? Join Penciljam for a 90-minute introduction to Sketch Journaling at MAP’s Living Botanicals exhibition.

Sketch journaling is a way of documenting the world around you through a combination of drawing, words, colours and observations. It’s about slowing down, looking a little closer and finding your own ways to record what catches your attention.

In this workshop, we’ll explore the ‘Living Botanicals‘ through our sketchbooks. You’ll try a few simple ways of observing and documenting what you see, combining drawings, handwritten notes and colour to create pages that are uniquely yours.You’ll leave with a few sketch journaling techniques, some new ways of looking at the world around you, and the beginnings of a visual journal of your own.
No previous drawing experience is necessary. Just bring your curiosity and a willingness to experiment!


 	A sketchbook or a few sheets of A4 paper with a pad
 	A pencil and eraser
 	A black fineliner or gel pen
 	Colour pencils, sketch pens or brush pens

Register here to attend. Free to attend, registration is needed.
